name: PDF annotation dictionaries
what_it_is: ISO 32000-1:2008 objects associated with locations on PDF pages. A page Annots array references annotation dictionaries; common fields include Subtype, Rect, Contents, name, modification date, flags, and optional appearance streams.
render_model: Viewer-native PDF objects. Conforming readers interpret annotation dictionaries and may render built-in appearances or an annotation's appearance stream over page content.
annotation_support: Native PDF markup. Highlight, Underline, Squiggly, and StrikeOut text-markup annotations require QuadPoints; markup dictionaries can carry author, pop-up, opacity, rich text, creation date, subject, and threaded reply links through IRT and RT.
coordinate_space: Rect and QuadPoints use default PDF user space. Text-markup QuadPoints contain 8 times n numbers for quadrilaterals around words or contiguous word groups; an appearance stream can take precedence over QuadPoints.
desktop_fit: Useful only for an explicit annotated-copy export or for displaying annotations already in the PDF. Native viewer appearance and interaction behavior can vary and does not replace Jevsume's application workflow.
mobile_fit: Viewer-dependent. PDF-native annotations can travel with an exported file, but touch targets, pop-ups, replies, and appearances are controlled by each mobile PDF reader rather than Jevsume.
overlay_chat_fit: Poor for the default live product because writing threads into IRT and RT relationships changes the PDF and constrains application metadata. Stronger as a deliberately requested interoperability export.
license: PDF 32000-1:2008 is a document-format standard published by ISO and hosted by Adobe; it is not a software library dependency. Implementations must observe the standard document's stated terms.
already_in_repo: No PDF mutation or annotation-dictionary writer is present. pdfjs-dist can read/render PDF annotations, while Jevsume's findings currently remain JSON text spans.
risks: Adding dictionaries, even incrementally, creates a changed PDF artifact; appearance streams may override geometry; viewer behavior differs; replies must be on the same page under the ISO model; permissions and digital signatures require special handling; silently editing an upload violates the product constraint.
recommendation: avoid for default storage — keep pins, regions, threads, and triggers in a non-mutating application overlay; only create a new, clearly labeled annotated PDF copy through a future explicit export flow.
uncertain: No annotated-copy export requirement is currently specified, so PDF-writing library selection and cross-viewer conformance testing are out of scope.
The uploaded PDFs' permission flags, certification signatures, and document modification policies are unknown and would need explicit checks before any export implementation.
ISO 32000-2 may add or refine annotation details, but PDF 1.7 is sufficient to establish that native markup is embedded document state rather than a non-mutating overlay.
